name: March 16, 2022 Special Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC FACILITIES AUTHORITY MEETING
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MARCH 16, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED – VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  1:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from
various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Greenstein called the meeting to order at 1:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance:

  PRESENT: Chair Nancy Greenstein; and Commissioners Margaret Quińones-
  Perez (arrived at 1:04 p.m.), Paul Grisanti, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) Members Steve
  McClary, City of Malibu (Malibu)Interim City Manager, and Dr. Kathryn Jeffery,
  Santa Monica College (SMC) Superintendent/President; Ruthie Quinto, Malibu
  Interim Assistant City Manager; Donald Girard, SMC Senior Director of
  Government Relations and Institutional Relations; Chris Bonvenuto, SMC Vice
  President of Administration and Business Services; Charlie Yen, SMC Director of
  Facilities Planning; Bradley Lane, SMC Vice President of Academic Affairs; Yu-
  Ngok Lo, Assistant Director of Facilities Planning Construction; Maral Hyeler,
  Director, SMC Instructional Services & External Programs; Shari Davis, Project
  Manager, SMC Special Projects; Kristin Riesgo, Malibu Community Services
  Deputy Director; Elizabeth Shavelson, Malibu Assistant to the City Manager
  Shavelson; Parker Davis, Malibu Media Technician; and Mary Linden, Malibu
  Executive Assistant

At the request of Commissioner Greenstein, MPFA members and staff introduced
themselves.

Commissioner Quińones-Perez arrived at 1:04 p.m.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Grisanti moved, and Commissioner Silverstein seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion
  carried unanimously.
   Malibu Public Facilities Authority
  Minutes of March 16, 2022
  Page 2 of 4
  __________________________

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Malibu Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  properly posted on March 14, 2022.

ITEM 1A  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 1B  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 2  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Quińones-Perez moved, and Commissioner Silverstein
  seconded a motion to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was
  called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:

  A.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended action: Approve minutes of the Malibu Public
  Facilities Authority meeting of December 8, 2021.

ITEM 3  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Santa Monica College Malibu Campus Community Outreach
  Recommended Action: Receive an update and provide feedback on Santa
  Monica College (SMC) plans for assessing community interest in
  educational programs and hosted events at the new SMC Malibu Campus.

  SMC Vice President of Academic Affairs Lane presented the report. He
  displayed the draft online Malibu Campus Survey. He reviewed the
  questions included in the survey.

  TAC Member McClary discussed the community events section. He stated
  many in the community were looking for locations where movies and other
  types of events could be offered. Mr. Lane stated the interpretive center
  space was indoors with a separate entrance and was flexible in design. He
  stated films would be more appropriate for the lecture hall.
   Malibu Public Facilities Authority
  Minutes of March 16, 2022
  Page 3 of 4
  __________________________

  In response to Commissioner Grisanti, SMC Director Yen confirmed the
  lecture hall could seat 96 people. Commissioner Grisanti asked when the
  survey would be released and how it would be communicated to the
  community.

  SMC Senior Director Girard stated a postcard would be sent to Malibu
  residents and businesses with the link to complete the survey online. He
  stated ads would be placed in The Malibu Times. He stated there would be
  community forums in May and October.

  Commissioner Grisanti asked if the City had an email list for Malibu
  residents. TAC Member McClary stated the City would assist with outreach
  through its various social media and communication channels.

  SMC Senior Director Girard stated information would also be sent to
  KBUU to be provided on the radio.

  Commissioner Greenstein stated the online survey would also provide
  residents with more information about possible offerings from SMC.

B.  Update on Santa Monica College Malibu Campus and Los Angeles County
  Sheriff Substation
  Recommended Action: Receive and file an update on the Santa Monica
  College Malibu Campus and Los Angeles County Sheriff Substation
  project. This project is not funded by the City of Malibu.

  SMC Director Yen provided a presentation on the status of the project.

  In response to Commissioner Greenstein, SMC Director Yen stated the roof
  included a deck, insulation, two layers of waterproofing, an inner layer, and
  a zinc roofing panel.

  SMC Director Yen stated the estimated completion was pushed back one
  month to November 2022 due to unforeseen COVID-19 shutdowns.

  Commissioner Greenstein asked about safety features in the college areas
  of the building. SMC Director Yen stated the Sheriff’s substation had
  security cameras, double-doors, secured parking in the back, away from the
  public. Commissioner Greenstein requested facts about security features be
  provided to alleviate any public concerns.

  Commissioner Grisanti asked if there were internal doors between the
  substation and the school area. SMC Director Yen stated there was one door
  for when the campus was used as an emergency operations center (EOC).
  In response to Commissioner Grisanti, SMC Director Yen confirmed all
  doors to the Sheriff’s station would be lockable.
   Malibu Public Facilities Authority
  Minutes of March 16, 2022
  Page 4 of 4
  __________________________

  TAC Member McClary inquired about the ownership of the property, in
  particular the Sheriff’s station. SMC Senior Director Girard stated the
  property was owned by the County of Los Angeles. He stated SMC had a
  99-year lease agreement with the County. He stated the Sheriff’s Substation
  was not included in that lease and would be solely owned by the County
  following construction. He stated there were arrangements in the lease for
  the Malibu Labor Exchange and the Malibu Farmers Market on Sundays.
  He stated the lease included a division of the parking lot in front of the
  library.

  SMC Director Yen stated the communications tower would arrive in April.
  In response to SMC Senior Director Girard, SMC Director Yen stated
  operation of the tower would be turned over to the County after construction
  was completed.

  SMC Special Projects Manager Davis requested feedback about signage in
  the parking lot.

  SMC Director Yen stated SMC submitted a request to the City regarding
  sign regulations. TAC Member McClary stated he would ask Planning staff
  to provide that information.

ITEM 5  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

  In response to Commissioner Greenstein, Commissioner Grisanti suggested
  meetings be scheduled every two months.

ITEM 6  CLOSED SESSION

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Commission adjourned the meeting at 1:40 p.m.

  Approved and adopted by the Malibu Public
  Facilities Authority on May 26, 2022.

  NANCY GREENSTEIN, Chair
